The '''2011–12 Scottish Premier League''' was the fourteenth season of the [[Scottish Premier League]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]], since its inception in 1998. The season started on 23 July 2011<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s2&newsid=9984 |publisher=Scottish Premier League |access-date=1 May 2011 |title=SPL Press Release: 2011/12 Season Start Date |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319173328/http://www.scotprem.com/content/default.asp?page=s2&newsid=9984 |archive-date=19 March 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> and ended on 13 May 2012.

A total of twelve teams contested the league: eleven sides that competed in the [[2010–11 Scottish Premier League|2010–11 SPL]] and one club promoted from the [[Scottish Football League First Division|First Division]]. The new entry was First Division champions [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], who replaced relegated [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].

Since Scotland climbed from sixteenth to fifteenth place in the [[UEFA coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of the 2010–11 season,<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Country Ranking 2011|url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2011.html|publisher=Bert Kassies|access-date=14 April 2011|archive-date=15 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110515233837/http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2011.html|url-status=live}}</ref> the league re-gained an additional third qualifying round berth for the [[UEFA Champions League]]. However, it lost that berth again the following season.  Despite finishing in the second qualifying position for the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League]], the [[Administration and liquidation of The Rangers Football Club plc|eventual liquidation]] of the company which owned [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] allowed [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] to take their place in the competition for the first time in the club's history.

On 7 April, [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] won the title after a 6–0 away win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at [[Rugby Park]]. It was their first title in four years.<ref>{{cite news
 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/9191876/Celtic-win-Scottish-Premier-League-title-with-6-0-victory-over-Kilmarnock.html

The team ending the 2010–11 season at the bottom of the table, [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], were relegated to the [[2011–12 Scottish First Division]]. Hamilton were replaced by [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], champions of the First Division.
